claim: The byte a page prints `Threshold` against is decibels, 0.4776 of them a step over two independent twenty-one step stretches that agree to 0.0009, and the limiting stops at byte 61.2 for the level this was read at, above which the four states of the ratio byte are one reading to 0.01 of a decibel. The type takes a further 2.7 decibels off whatever it is doing, constant across thirty decibels of input and therefore not limiting. Of the four states of the byte printed `Ratio`, only the one printed `1/100` behaves as a ratio: its gain reduction is proportional to how far the signal sits over the threshold to a part in a thousand. The other three do not. Walked as a ladder instead -- the level going in moved thirty-six decibels at one setting of the threshold byte, which uses no part of that byte -- each of the four states returns a slope, and one minus that slope comes back 0.2499, 0.5052, 0.7518 and 0.9947: a quarter, a half, three quarters and all of the level over the threshold, to within a part in a hundred. The page names the middle two of those correctly and the outer two not. The state printed `1/1.5` takes three quarters of the level away where two thirds is printed against it, and the state printed `1/100` holds its output still to a hundredth of a decibel over eight decibels of input, where one part in a hundred would have moved it eight times the run's own floor. What the sentence before this one says of the other three is about their gain reduction being proportional to the distance over the threshold, which is a different quantity from the slope: each of them still takes six to eight and a half tenths of a decibel off where the signal sits at the threshold, so the line they follow does not pass through it. Walked as a ladder instead -- the level going in moved thirty-six decibels at one setting of the threshold byte, which uses no part of that byte -- each of the four states returns a slope, and one minus that slope comes back 0.2499, 0.5052, 0.7518 and 0.9947: a quarter, a half, three quarters and all of the level over the threshold, to within a part in a hundred. The page names the middle two of those correctly and the outer two not. The state printed `1/1.5` takes three quarters of the level away where two thirds is printed against it, and the state printed `1/100` holds its output still to a hundredth of a decibel over eight decibels of input, where one part in a hundred would have moved it eight times the run's own floor. Four fixed ratios of one quantity make the gain reductions a rank one table, whose columns would stand in one proportion; measured, that proportion walks from 1.682 to 1.523 across the four states, and the ratio each of the three returns changes with how far over the threshold it is asked.
why_not_named: A limiter is what the page calls it and what the readings are consistent with, and naming it would add nothing this claim does not already say. What would be worth naming -- the shape of the knee that makes three of the four states behave as they do -- is exactly what has not been read: three thresholds is not enough points to fit a knee to, and a name put on it now would be the part retracted first.

measurements.why: The threshold byte at seven values with the ratio byte held at the state the page prints 1/1.5 against. Four records rather than one because the ratio byte is in the held block and a record carries one swept address; what the claim is read off is the four of them together and nothing inside any one.

The threshold byte at seven values with the ratio byte held at the state the page prints 1/2 against. Four records rather than one because the ratio byte is in the held block and a record carries one swept address; what the claim is read off is the four of them together and nothing inside any one.

The threshold byte at seven values with the ratio byte held at the state the page prints 1/4 against. Four records rather than one because the ratio byte is in the held block and a record carries one swept address; what the claim is read off is the four of them together and nothing inside any one.

The threshold byte at seven values with the ratio byte held at the state the page prints 1/100 against. Four records rather than one because the ratio byte is in the held block and a record carries one swept address; what the claim is read off is the four of them together and nothing inside any one.

The part's own volume walked down about thirty decibels with the threshold byte at the top of its range, each rung taken both through the effect and past it. This is what says the constant the type takes off above the knee is a loss and not limiting the threshold byte cannot reach: a loss does not move when the input drops and a gain reduction does. The section was not in the run as designed and was added from the run's own first sweep.

document_rows.why: That these two addresses are a threshold and a ratio, that the second has four states, and the four numbers the four states are held against. The page prints no unit beside the threshold, so what a step of it is worth is measured here and not read.

era_priors.claim: A stage of this period computes its gain from a level detector through a short table rather than from a logarithm, so a ratio exact in decibels is the expensive case and a ratio exact only far from the threshold is the ordinary one.
era_priors.why: It says why three of four states might depart from a printed number in the same direction while the fourth does not: a state that clamps needs no ratio arithmetic at all and can be exact for free.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: One of the three departing states came back exact in decibels somewhere in its range while the clamping one did not. The prior is about which of the four is cheap to get right, and that ordering is the whole of it.

adds: Each record says what the level was at each setting of the threshold byte under one state of the ratio byte. What is read out of them here is what no one of them holds: that the four together are not four multipliers of one quantity. The scale of the threshold byte in decibels is read off the state that is linear in it, the other three are then held against that scale, and the departure is a comparison across four records. The ladder adds the second thing none of the sweeps can say, because the byte it would have to be said with has run out of range.

alternatives.reading: The four states are four fixed ratios and the departure from them is in the reading rather than in the unit.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The repeats of one setting agree at the first order to 0.0 of a decibel, and the four states above the knee agree to 0.01. The departure is one and a half decibels, which is two orders larger than either. The whole order series moves together as well, so it is a gain that is being read and not a shape.

alternatives.reading: The threshold byte is not linear in decibels, and the three states curve because the axis they are read against does.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The axis is read off the fourth state, whose gain reduction is straight in the byte over both stretches -- 0.4776 and 0.4767 decibels a step. A bent axis would bend that state too, and it is the state with the most of the axis in it.

alternatives.reading: The threshold byte does not move a threshold. It sets how much of the level over a fixed threshold is taken, so what looks like three states departing is the two bytes doing one job between them.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The part's own volume was walked down thirty-six decibels at three settings of the threshold byte on each of two states of the ratio byte. This reading requires the three gain reduction curves of one state to be one curve times a constant, so that their quotient is one number at every input; measured on the arm printed `1/100` that quotient is 0.700, 0.657, 0.604, 0.531, 0.342, 0.003 and 0.006 down the ladder, where this reading needs 0.657 at all seven. Fitted as a vertical scale it leaves 1.70 to 3.05 decibels on the four comparisons; fitted as a sideways move it leaves 0.03 to 0.48, against eight rungs that repeat to 0.010. The move is also the same on both states of the ratio byte -- 9.96 against 9.95, and 20.09 against 20.09 -- which is what a quantity the ratio byte is not part of looks like.

alternatives.reading: The state printed `1/1.5` is a ratio like the other three, and what is a quarter away is the reading of it rather than the state.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It is not. The ladder and the threshold sweep share no quantity -- one is the output against the level going in at a fixed byte, the other is gain reduction against the byte at a fixed level -- and the ladder returns 0.2499 where the sweep's chord converts to 0.2469. What the page prints against that state is 0.3333, which is five times the spread the other three states' fits show and twenty-five times what two independent readings of this one disagree by.

alternatives.reading: The four states are the page's table with two of its four entries wrong, rather than four even quarter steps of one quantity.

separated_by.observable: Nothing this unit's output can be asked. The two readings return the same four numbers.

predicts.four even quarter steps: a quarter, a half, three quarters, all
predicts.the page's table with two entries wrong: a quarter, a half, three quarters, all

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The ladder routed past the effect repeats to 0.010 of a decibel across the run's eight directories, and it bounds nothing here: the two readings do not differ in any quantity, so no floor applies to the difference.
separated_by.why_not_separable: They return the same four numbers. Even quarter steps of one quantity and the page's table with two of its four entries wrong both give a quarter, a half, three quarters and all, because the middle two entries are printed as a half and a quarter already. Nothing that comes out of this unit distinguishes a byte indexing four even fractions from a byte indexing a table that happens to hold them, which is the same shape the level class parked for the same reason. What argues for the steps is the era and not a measurement -- two bits and one multiply against a four entry table -- and a prior may carry a claim and may not close one.

refuted_by: The state printed `1/100` ceasing to be straight in the threshold byte somewhere in its range, which would take away the axis every other figure here is held against. Or the decibels a step coming back different at another input level, which would say the byte is not a threshold. Or the constant the type takes off above the knee moving with the input, which would make it limiting rather than a loss.
what_this_does_not_settle: What the other three states are. They separate in the order the page prints and each is monotone in the threshold byte, but the ratio each returns changes with how far over the threshold it is asked -- the first state returns [0.718, 0.744, 0.642] against a printed 0.667 -- and three thresholds is not enough to fit a shape to.

Whether the three approach their printed numbers far enough over the threshold. The furthest this run reached is 29.2 decibels over, and the input cannot be raised more than about four decibels further on this unit without leaving the level every other take in this archive was made at.
What the release byte does. It was held at the value the type powers up at throughout, and a reading taken on the settled body of an eight second tone cannot see a time constant.
Where the constant loss sits relative to the limiting. The ladder says it is not limiting and says nothing about whether it is before or after the stage that is.

Only the state printed `1/100` returns a slope that settles. Read segment by segment down the ladder the other three walk: the state printed `1/1.5` returns 0.214, 0.295, 0.397, 0.182, 0.191, 0.282, 0.352 and 0.425 against a fitted 0.2499, and the state printed `1/2` returns 0.470, 0.585, 0.686, 0.381, 0.438, 0.596 and 0.394 against a fitted 0.5052. The walk is not noise -- the ladder routed past the effect repeats to 0.010 of a decibel across eight directories and the swing here is a tenth of a slope -- and it has a shape: the figure climbs over consecutive rungs and drops back where the step between rungs widens. What that is of is not established. It does not change how any record here is read, so it is written down where it was found and not followed.

The three states that are not a wall still take six to eight and a half tenths of a decibel off at the input the wall reaches nothing at -- 0.62, 0.85 and 0.74 going from the deepest to the shallowest -- and the wall takes none. A knee with a width would put the most there on the state that takes the most, and this is the other way round. Not explained here.
what_it_would_change: Two of the eight printed parameters of a type that carried no structural reading at all. A renderer given this type can put its threshold where the byte asks and knows that one of its four ratio settings is the printed number and that three of them are not -- which is the difference between approximating the stage and knowing which part of it is approximate.

the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.the_reading_this_answers: The threshold byte does not move a threshold. It sets how much of the level over a fixed threshold is taken, so what looks like three states departing is the two bytes doing one job between them.

the_booking_this_answers.observable: The part's own volume walked down at a low setting of the threshold byte, on each of the four states of the ratio byte. The ladder in this claim was taken at the top of the threshold byte, where nothing is limited, so it does not reach this.

predicts.a threshold: The gain reduction depends only on how far the signal sits over the threshold, so lowering the input ten decibels at a held threshold returns what the sweep returned ten decibels further up its own axis -- for the first state, 4.9 decibels.
predicts.an amount: The gain reduction is set by the byte, so it stays near 8.24 decibels as the input drops.

the_booking_this_answers.divergence: 3.34 decibels on the first state, and more on the other three.
the_booking_this_answers.sensitivity_here: The repeats of one setting agree at the first order to 0.0 of a decibel on a ladder of this shape already taken on this type.

run.stimulus: The held tone this type was read on, program 16 at note 81, with the part's own volume walked down instead of a byte: 127, 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20.
run.why:
One directory per state of the ratio byte, the threshold byte held at nought so that the stage is working, and the part's own volume walked down about thirty decibels with every rung taken through the effect and past it. The same shape as `limiter-ladder` in this run's own driver with the threshold byte moved and a directory per ratio state.

What it separates is whether the threshold byte moves a threshold. Under a static curve the gain reduction depends only on how far the signal sits over the threshold, so reaching a distance by dropping the input has to return what reaching it by raising the threshold returned. Nothing in this run reaches that, because the only ladder in it was taken where the stage is passing the signal.

the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.what_came_back: The three ladders of one state of the ratio byte are one ladder moved sideways, and the move is the same on both states. Fitted against the deepest setting of the threshold byte, twenty-one steps of it move the ladder 9.96 decibels along the input axis on the arm printed `1/100` and 9.95 on the arm printed `1/2`, and forty-two steps move it 20.09 on both. What the move leaves is 0.03 to 0.48 of a decibel; what a vertical scale leaves on the same points is 1.70 to 3.05. The reading the run was booked against needs the quotient of two ladders to be one number at every input, and it stands at 0.700 where the input is loudest and 0.003 five rungs down.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.the_decibels_a_step_measured_on_its_own: The claim's decibels a step were read as a vertical distance -- how much gain reduction a step of the byte adds at one input -- and turning that into decibels needed the arm printed `1/100` to be a true hundredth, which nothing in that run could test. Here the same quantity is a horizontal distance: how far the input has to move to undo a step of the byte, which is what a threshold is whatever the ratio does. The two stretches give 0.4743 and 0.4824 decibels a step on one arm and 0.4738 and 0.4829 on the other, against 0.4776 and 0.4767 published. They agree to four thousandths of a decibel a step, and the second reading rests on nothing the first one assumed.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.the_floor_this_run_had: Better than any the claim has quoted. The ladder routed past the effect is the same eight takes in all six directories -- the bytes under test are not in that path -- so it was measured six times from six separate preparations of the unit, and its eight rungs agree to 0.010 of a decibel. Each directory also carries its own repeats, which agree in the band to 0.00 to 0.02, and its own silence, which every reading here stands at least 26.9 decibels over. The channel was named rather than chosen by level in all six, which is what the neighbouring run got wrong in the one directory where the state under test was the quietest thing in it.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.the_knee_is_reported_and_is_not_the_read: Where each ladder stops limiting is reported and is not what separates the two readings. Read as the input the gain reduction crosses half a decibel at, the three land 11.77 and 7.64 decibels apart on one arm and 11.67 and 8.20 on the other, where the sideways move says 9.96 and 10.13. The difference is this reading's own: the rungs are four to six decibels apart and a crossing is read by straight line between two of them, so where the curve bends the crossing is pulled towards the wider gap. The fit uses every rung of the curve and does not need the crossing, which is why it was written as the test before the run rather than after it.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.the_ratio_read_as_a_ladder: The slope of the output against the input above the knee is what a compression ratio is, and it uses no part of the threshold byte. The arm printed `1/100` holds its output inside 0.17 of a decibel while the input falls 29.7, which is a slope of 0.0053 where an exact hundredth would give 0.0100 -- harder than it prints. The arm printed `1/2` returns 0.4948 over the same stretch on seven rungs, which is its printed number to one part in a hundred.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.what_this_does_to_the_run_that_raised_th: It converts its table without any further hardware, which is why only two of the four states were walked. That run measured four slopes of gain reduction against the threshold byte and could only normalise them against each other; divided by the decibels a step measured here they become four ratios. Three of the four land on the numbers the page prints -- the states printed `1/2`, `1/4` and `1/100` come back inside one and a half per cent -- and the state printed `1/1.5` comes back a quarter away. That is not the same statement as the one the claim's own sentence makes, and this round does not rewrite it: three of these four are chords of a curve rather than slopes of a line, and only two of the four have a ladder. What the conversion is good for is saying which state to walk next, and it says the two that were not walked here.
the_round_that_walked_the_input_at_three.what_the_ladders_show_and_do_not_settle: The arm printed `1/100` is straight: its six segments above the knee return 0.993 to 1.000 of the input. The arm printed `1/2` is not. Its segments run from 0.32 to 0.69 about a mean of 0.505, and its gain reduction is not proportional to how far the signal sits over the threshold but carries about seven tenths of a decibel where that distance is nothing. Against a ladder that repeats to 0.010 of a decibel neither of those is noise. What they are of is not established here -- a knee with a width, a table the gain is read out of, or something else -- and three thresholds and eight rungs are not enough to put a shape on it. It is written down where it was found.

the_round_that_walked_the_two_states_tha.the_reading_this_answers: The state printed `1/1.5` is a ratio like the other three, and what is a quarter away is the reading of it rather than the state.

the_booking_this_answers.observable: The part's own volume walked down at the bottom of the threshold byte on the two states of the ratio byte that have no ladder, read as the slope of the output against the input above the knee -- the same reading the two states here were read by.

predicts.a ratio like the other three: the state printed `1/1.5` returns a slope of 0.667

the_booking_this_answers.divergence: 0.086 of slope, which over the thirty-three decibels this state stands above its threshold at the bottom of the threshold byte is 2.9 decibels of output.
the_booking_this_answers.sensitivity_here: The ladder routed past the effect was measured six times from six separate preparations of the unit in the run this round is of, and its eight rungs agreed to 0.010 of a decibel.

run.stimulus: The held tone this type is read on, program 16 at note 81, with the part's own volume walked down through 127, 100, 80, 64, 45, 32, 23 and 16 -- every rung taken through the effect and past it, the threshold byte at nought.
run.why: Two of the four states now have a ladder and their slopes are the ratio read directly. The other two have only a chord of the threshold sweep, and on the three states whose gain reduction is not proportional to the distance over the threshold a chord is not a slope. The state printed `1/1.5` is the one where the two disagree by enough to see, and the state printed `1/4` comes with it because the same ladder answers both and a run that walked only the state that disagreed would be a run chosen after the fact.

the_round_that_walked_the_two_states_tha.what_came_back: The two states that had no ladder have one. One minus the slope comes back 0.2499 on the state printed `1/1.5` and 0.7518 on the state printed `1/4`, against 0.5052 and 0.9947 on the two walked before them. Read against the page's four numbers that is one state a quarter away and three inside half a per cent; read as four even quarter steps of one quantity it is four states inside one per cent. Both readings have no free parameter in them, and they give the same number at the states printed `1/2` and `1/4`.
the_round_that_walked_the_two_states_tha.the_two_states_that_decide_and_the_two_t: Two of the four carry no information here and are named so rather than counted. A half and three quarters are what the page prints and what even quarter steps give, so a state landing on one of them agrees with both readings and separates nothing. What the reading rests on is the other two. The state printed `1/1.5` returns 0.2499 where the page asks for 0.3333 -- five times the spread the other three fits show. The state printed `1/100` returns 1.0000 twice over, on the two segments of its ladder furthest from the knee, where the page asks for 0.9900.
the_round_that_walked_the_two_states_tha.the_state_printed_one_hundredth_is_a_wal: The state printed `1/100` does not let its output move at all. Over the three loudest rungs it comes back at -80.54, -80.54 and -80.54 decibels full scale while the level going in falls 8.03, so the slope is 0.0000 on two consecutive segments. A ratio of one part in a hundred would have moved it 0.08 of a decibel there, which is eight times what the ladder routed past the effect repeats to across this run's eight directories. Read over the whole limiting stretch the same arm gives 0.9947 rather than 1.0000, and that is the knee being inside the fit: the segments nearest it return 0.9844 and 0.5480.
the_round_that_walked_the_two_states_tha.what_the_booking_got_right_and_what_it_g: The entry that booked this run named two numbers for the state printed `1/1.5` -- 0.667 if it is the ratio its page prints and 0.753 if it is what the threshold sweep's chord converts to. It came back 0.7501. The chord and the ladder share no quantity: one is gain reduction against a byte at a fixed input and the other is output against input at a fixed byte, and they agree to three thousandths. What the entry had wrong was its margin, which divided a difference between two fitted slopes by the floor of a level. The separation actually achieved is 0.083 of slope against 0.017 of fitting spread, which is a margin of five.

the_figures.why_the_wall_reads_below_one_over_the_wh: Fitted over its whole limiting stretch the state printed `1/100` gives 0.9947, which is nearer the page's 0.9900 than the quarter step's 1.0000 -- and the fit has the knee inside it. Each arm's segments are published beside this figure and that state's two furthest from the knee both give 1.0000, while the two nearest give 0.9844 and 0.5480. The reading that separates the page from the quarter step on this state is the segment and not the fit, because a ratio is what the stage does far over the threshold and the fit averages in what it does at it.
